  "CRITERIA_MATCH_EXPLANATION": "The paper focuses on regional curriculum harmonization initiatives in East Africa, specifically examining the EAC (East African Community) framework. It addresses harmonization across institutions and countries within the EAC region, discussing mutual recognition, credit transfer systems, and regional qualifications frameworks. The paper explicitly mentions the EAC Protocol on Education and Training and its implications for cross-border education.",
  "Title": "Harmonisation of Higher Education Curricula in East Africa: A Synthesis of Selected Literature",

    "Theoretical_Framework": "Not explicitly stated, but implicitly draws on theories of regional integration and education policy.",

  "KEY_FINDINGS": {
    "Main_Findings": [
      "Harmonization of higher education curricula in East Africa is crucial for regional integration and economic development.",
      "The EAC Protocol on Education and Training provides a framework for harmonization, but implementation faces challenges.",
      "Mutual recognition of qualifications and credit transfer systems are essential for student mobility.",
      "Quality assurance mechanisms are needed to ensure the comparability of qualifications across institutions and countries."
    ],

      "Involvement of all stakeholders",
      "Capacity building"

      "Strengthen political commitment to harmonization.",
      "Increase funding for harmonization initiatives.",
      "Improve coordination among stakeholders.",
      "Build capacity in higher education institutions.",
      "Develop robust quality assurance mechanisms."
    ],
    "Future_Research": [
      "Further research is needed to evaluate the impact of harmonization on student mobility and graduate employability.",
      "Research is also needed to identify best practices for harmonization in different disciplines."
